title: Altimeter
src: R.K. Bali — Air Navigation, Part II Ch 2

qs.q: A servo altimeter has a quoted accuracy of 1 hPa at mean sea level. The accuracy in the standard atmosphere is:
o: +- 50 ft at 10 000 ft and +- 100 ft at 40 000 f
+- 50 ft at 20 000 ft and +- 90 ft at the tropopause
+- 27 ft at MSL and +- 50 ft at 10 000 ft
qs.ex: 1 hPa ≈ 27 ft near MSL; the same 1 hPa is a bigger height step higher up (≈ 50 ft at 10 000 ft).

What will happen if an a/c has 2 altimeters, one of which is compensated for position error, whilst the other is not:
o: One will over read at high air speed
One will under read at high air speed
One will under read close to the ground.

qs.q: The purpose of stand by static source is:
If static source of an a/c is blocked in unpressurised a/c the correct action for pilot will be:
qs.ex: Book note: the altimeter glass is never broken; the VSI glass is broken in an emergency because it is less important. Where an alternate static source exists, use it.

qs.q: White zebra crossing on the altimeter appears when:
o: a/c is below MSA (minimum safe altitude)

qs.q: When flying from a sector of warm air into one of colder air, the altimeter will?
o: Show the actual height above ground.

qs.q: Temp. error in altimeter is caused due to:
o: Non standard temp at a/c altitude

qs.q: Bimetallic strip in altimeter is provided
o: To compensate for thermal expansion of mechanical linkages.
To compensate for adiabatic rise in temperature of temp error.

qs.q: Pressure error in an altimeter arises because:
o: The true external dynamic pressure is not accurately transmitted to the instrument
The true external static pressure is not accurately transmitted to the instrument
The true external kinetic pressure is not accurately transmitted to the instrument

qs.q: In a non-pressurized aircraft, if one or several static pressure ports are damaged, there is an ultimate emergency means for restoring a practically correct static pressure intake:
o: breaking the rate-of-climb indicator glass window
Slightly opening a window to restore the ambient pressure in the cabin
calculating the ambient static pressure, allowing for the altitude and QNH adjusting the instruments

qs.q: The pressure altitude is the altitude corresponding:
o: in ambient atmosphere, to the reference pressure Ps
in standard atmosphere, to the reference pressure Ps
in standard atmosphere, to the pressure Ps prevailing at this point

qs.q: The altimeter consists of several aneroid capsules located in a sealed casing. The pressure in the aneroid capsule (i) and casing (ii) are respectively:
o: (i) static pressure at time t (ii) static pressure at time t − Δt
(i) vacuum (or a very low pressure) (ii) static pressure

qs.q: Altimeter gives height of aircraft with respect to :
We are maintaining a constant flight level. That means:
o: the outside air pressure is constant if the temperature remains constant
the outside air pressure is constant
the altitude is constant when the sea-level pressure is constant

qs.q: The altitude indicated on board an aircraft flying in an atmosphere where all atmosphere layers below the aircraft are warm is:
o: the same as the real altitude
qs.ex: Printed key (b). Note the physics: in WARM air an altimeter under-reads (true altitude is higher than indicated) — 'indicated higher than real' is the COLD-air case. Learn the book answer for this exact wording, but know the rule: hot to cold, look out below.

qs.q: In case of accidental closing of an aircraft's left static pressure port (rain, birds), the altimeter:
o: Over reads the altitude in case of a sideslip to the left and and displays the correct information during symmetric flight
keeps on providing reliable reading in all sitations
qs.ex: In a left sideslip the clear right port is on the lee side, sensing lower pressure → over-read. In balanced flight the remaining port reads correctly.

qs.q: The altimeter is fed by:
The advantage of sensitive altimeter over service altimeter is.
o: It does not form lag error.
It can be used up to higher altitude

qs.q: The error in altimeter readings caused by the variation of the static pressure near the source is known as:
If the static source of an altimeter becomes blocked during a descent the instrument will:
o: continue to display the reading at which the blockage occurred
qs.ex: A blocked static source traps the pressure: the altimeter freezes at the reading when the blockage occurred.

qs.q: The primary factor which makes the servo-assisted altimeter more accurate than the simple pressure altimeter is the use of:
o: more effective temperature compensating leaf springs

qs.q: At sea level, on a typical servo altimeter, the tolerance in feet from indicated must not exceed:
An aircraft is flying straight and level, over a warm air mass. The altimeter reading will be:
qs.ex: Warm air: pressure levels sit higher, so the aircraft is higher than indicated → reading less than real height.

qs.q: When flying from a sector of warm air into one of colder air, the altimeter will:
o: be just as correct as before

qs.q: The hysteresis error of an altimeter varies substantially with the:
o: time passed at a given altitude

The purpose of the vibrating device of an altimeter is to?
o: Allow damping of the measurement in the unit.
Reduce the effect of friction in the linkages.

qs.q: Lag error in servo assisted altimeter is virtually removed by:
o: Using more than one capsule in series.

In an aircraft a static source is so placed that it is having subjected to dynamic pressure. The error caused of any will be known as:
The principle of operation of a servo-assisted pressure altimeter is that:
o: static pressure is used in the same way as a simple altimeter except that several capsules are used
static pressure changes are converted via an E- and 1-bar transducer into electrical signal which is used, via a follow-up system, to move a digital counter and pointer system
static pressure enters an aneroid capsule causing it to expand

qs.q: When flying from low pressure to high pressure, the barometric error of an altimeter will cause the instrument to:
o: indicate a higher altitude than the correct one.
Under read the true altitude of the aircraft.
qs.ex: Low → high pressure without resetting: the altimeter under-reads (aircraft higher than indicated). High → low: over-reads ('high to low, look out below').

qs.q: What will happen to the altimeter reading in a right sideslip, if an aircraft has a static vent at each side of the fuselage, but the left one is blocked?
qs.ex: Right sideslip: the clear right port faces the airflow → higher pressure → under-read.

qs.q: A barometric altimeter comprises of?
o: An aneroid capsule sensing static pressure.
An aneroid capsule sensing pitot pressure.
A differential capsule sensing pitot and static pressures.

qs.q: What will happen to the altimeter reading in a right sideslip, if an aircraft has a static vent at each side of the fuselage, but the right one is blocked?
qs.ex: Right sideslip with the right port blocked: the clear left port is on the lee side → lower pressure → over-read.

qs.q: The altimeter of an aircraft with a static pressure source on each side of the fuselage will if one becomes blocked?
o: Over read when side slipping towards the blocked source.
Over read when side slipping towards the clear source.

In a barometric altimeter, ______ is fed into the capsule and ______ is fed into the case?
If the static pressure source in an unpressurised aircraft became blocked, the altimeter would ______ but might be rectified by ______?
o: Read zero; break the altimeter glass

qs.q: If the pitot source becomes blocked the barometric altimeter will?
If the static vent becomes partly blocked in a descent the indications will?
o: Be too high when descending but correct when at constant altitude.
Be too high when descending but correct when at constant height.
Be too low when descending but correct when at constant altitude.
